channel.title: Claude AI Daily Brief
channel.description: Daily intelligence report on Claude AI news, Anthropic announcements, developer updates, and community buzz.

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 25, 2026
item.description:
1. Sonnet 4.5 Retires September 29 — Five weeks to migrate before API calls on the old identifier fail hard, the same pattern that hit Sonnet 4 and Opus 4 in June and Opus 4.1 on August 5.

2. Claude Code 2.1.243 Is an Emergency Linux Fix — Patches a startup crash on glibc 2.44 distros including Arch, CachyOS and Fedora Rawhide; 2.1.242 made /cost report contracted rates instead of list price.

3. Enterprise Gets Inference Hooks and Skill Scanning — Prompts and tool calls can now be inspected before they reach the model across chat, Claude Code and Cowork, with third-party skills and plugins scanned for malicious content.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 24, 2026
item.description:
1. Claude Goes Down Again, Sixth Time This Month — Elevated errors opened at 05:06 UTC across Mythos 5, Fable 5, Opus 5 and Opus 4.8, with partial outages on claude.ai, the API, Claude Code and Cowork.

2. The September 1 Price Increase Is Cancelled — Sonnet 5 stays at $2/$10 per million tokens permanently; the scheduled move to $3/$15 will not happen.

3. Every Claude Output Now Carries a Watermark — Machine-readable marking is live on all products shipped since August 2, worldwide, with older models covered by December 2.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 23, 2026
item.description:
1. Mythos 5 Starts Scanning Enterprise Code — The cyber model gated to vetted defenders since April now runs vulnerability scans inside Claude Security, billed as normal token usage, with every patch gated on human review.

2. $35 Million in Credits for Open-Source Defense — The new Defender Advantage Fund pays organizations in Claude credits to patch live vulnerabilities in widely used projects, on top of Project Glasswing’s $100M.

3. Anthropic Hires the Man Who Built Google’s TPU — Bloomberg reports Amir Salek, founder of Google’s custom silicon program and shipper of TPUv1 through v4, joined the compute team as Anthropic works toward its own chips.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 22, 2026
item.description:
1. MCP Publishes a New Roadmap — Five priority areas, led by agent identity via DPoP and Workload Identity Federation, and progressive tool discovery for servers with hundreds of tools.

2. Anthropic’s Ode Makes Its First Acquisition — The services venture backed by Blackstone and Goldman bought Casper Studios, a consultancy that wires Claude into existing enterprise systems, one month after launching.

3. The Python SDK Hits 1.0, and It Breaks Things — httpx becomes httpx2, Python 3.10 is the floor, and Text Completions plus temperature/top_p/top_k on Messages methods are removed.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 21, 2026
item.description:
1. Anthropic Tells Investors the IPO Will Match or Beat SpaceX — That means clearing $75 billion raised at a $1.77 trillion valuation; the CFO is reportedly declining to name a number in briefings.

2. The 30-Day Retention Mandate Finally Bends — A new safety system keeps the requirement for covered models but lets enterprises hold that data in their own cloud, designed with 100+ customers including Salesforce.

3. A Browser Use Toolset Lands, and Computer Use Goes GA — browser_toolset_20260801 gives Claude 27 browser tools that run entirely on your infrastructure, while computer use drops its beta header.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 20, 2026
item.description:
1. Claude Code Ships a “Concise” Output Style — v2.1.237 adds a built-in mode where Claude leads with results and skips the preamble, without cutting the work itself; select it under Output style in /config.

2. Three Betas Go GA in One Day — The Files API, Agent Skills and the Skills API, and Admin API user management all left beta, retiring three beta headers while old requests keep working unchanged.

3. Managed Agents Get Domain Allowlists — Agents can now be restricted to specific sites for web_search and web_fetch, plus memory stores in self-hosted sandboxes and a rebuilt Console session viewer.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 19, 2026
item.description:
1. The Usage Boost Expires Today — Claude Code’s temporary 50% weekly increase runs out today with no third extension announced; ceilings return to standard tomorrow.

2. Another Degraded-Performance Day — Elevated errors on Opus 5 and Haiku 4.5 follow seven separate incidents between August 12 and 16, including a 42-minute multi-service outage.

3. Cowork Lands in the Chrome Side Panel — Skills, plugins and connectors now work in the browser for the first time with no extra setup.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 18, 2026
item.description:
1. Revenue Run Rate Passes $65 Billion — Preliminary Q2 revenue topped $11.5 billion, a 14x jump year over year, with positive adjusted operating income and investors modeling $100–120 billion by year end.

2. Anthropic Raised Its Own Risk Rating — The August risk report moves catastrophic misalignment from very low to low, driven by uncertainty rather than a failed test, and discloses an unreleased internal model more capable than Mythos 5.

3. The Usage Boost Ends Tomorrow — Claude Code’s temporary 50% weekly increase runs through August 19 with no sign of a third extension; size your plan against the standard ceiling before Thursday.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 17, 2026
item.description:
1. Workbench Goes Dark Today — The legacy Workbench and the three experimental prompt tools endpoints retire today, taking saved prompts, versions and evals with them; export from the Console before you do anything else.

2. The September Price Hike Is Cancelled — Sonnet 5’s introductory $2/$10 per million tokens is now permanent, killing the 50% increase that was scheduled for September 1.

3. A 42-Minute Auth Outage Hit Five Services — Sign-ins failed across claude.ai, Console, the API, Claude Code and Cowork from 21:58 to 22:40 UTC Sunday, an auth-layer failure with no graceful fallback.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 16, 2026
item.description:
1. Workbench Retires Tomorrow — The legacy Workbench and the three experimental prompt tools endpoints go dark August 17, taking saved prompts, prompt versions and evals with them; export from the Console before then.

2. The IPO Roadshow Is Open — Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley are leading an October Nasdaq listing expected to raise more than $60 billion, with institutional meetings running through September.

3. Two Clocks Run Out This Week — Claude Code’s 50% weekly usage boost expires August 19, and the $1-per-agency Claude for Government program closes at month’s end.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 15, 2026
item.description:
1. Claude Fired a Human Worker — In an Andon Labs experiment running a real San Francisco store, Claude terminated an employee late for 17 of 23 shifts — but only after a manager’s leading question pushed it past its own recommendation of a written warning.

2. Q2 Revenue Hits $11.5 Billion — Up from $787M a year ago and $4.73B last quarter, with positive adjusted operating income, as backers point to an October IPO targeting $2 trillion or higher.

3. August Risk Report Raises Misalignment to “Low” — Anthropic also disclosed that 133 million human-feedback exchanges with 50,000 contractors ran without its blocking biological classifiers attached.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 14, 2026
item.description:
1. Auto Mode Is Now the Claude Code Default — The switch flipped today for Pro, Max, and Team. Anthropic’s data: the classifier blocked 89% of dangerous commands versus 13.6% for humans clicking approve.

2. Sonnet 5’s $2/$10 Pricing Is Permanent — Anthropic canceled the September 1 increase to $3/$15, erasing a 50% bill hike for high-volume API users.

3. Claude Tag Gets Free Proactive Replies — Claude in Slack now reads full channel context, memory, and standing instructions to decide when to speak, and is ~30% better at knowing when to stay quiet.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 13, 2026
item.description:
1. Claude Code Auto Mode Goes Default Tomorrow — Starting August 14, new Pro, Max, and Team sessions default to auto mode, where a safety classifier vets each tool call — and Anthropic won't charge for the extra compute.

2. Anthropic Loosens Fable 5's Biology Safeguards — Updated safety systems cut false-positive refusals on biology prompts by ~85%, while genuine dual-use research stays gated to Opus 5.

3. New Claude Models Now Watermark Their Text — Machine-readable watermarks are baked into output from new models to satisfy Article 50 of the EU AI Act.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 12, 2026
item.description:
1. Opus 5 Becomes Claude Code's Default — The latest release makes Opus 5 the default model, adds a Claude Security plugin for vulnerability scanning, and drops an iOS Simulator pane into Claude Code Desktop.

2. Compliance API Expands to Cowork and Claude Code — Enterprise security teams can now pull unified session content and metadata across desktop, web, mobile, and CLI for audits and eDiscovery.

3. Sonnet 5's Promo Pricing Ends August 31 — The $2/$10 per-million-token intro rate reverts to standard $3/$15 on September 1.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 11, 2026
item.description:
1. Anthropic Will Watermark All Claude Text — Worldwide — To meet the EU AI Act, every Claude model launched after August 2 gets invisible text watermarks and C2PA file provenance, applied globally, not just in Europe.

2. Claude Code Auto Mode Becomes the Default on August 14 — Pro, Max, and Team plans switch from manual approval prompts to a classifier that screens every tool call, pausing only for irreversible or destructive actions.

3. The MCP 2026-07-28 Spec Lands in Claude — A stateless, serverless-friendly core plus versioned Apps and Tasks extensions, with the connectors directory now past 950 MCP servers.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 10, 2026
item.description:
1. Claude Code Sessions Can Now Run on Your Own Infrastructure — Self-hosted environments hit public beta for Team and Enterprise, keeping checkouts, secrets, and build artifacts on machines you provision.

2. Microsoft 365 Connector Gains Write Tools — Claude can now draft and send email, manage calendar events, and create or update files in OneDrive and SharePoint, not just read them.

3. MCP Passes 400M Monthly SDK Downloads — Up 4x this year, with MCP tunnels in research preview so Claude can reach servers inside a private network with no public endpoint.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 9, 2026
item.description:
1. Enterprise Gains Model-Level Entitlements and Spend Alerts — Admins can now gate access model by model across Opus 5, Sonnet 5, and Haiku, with richer usage analytics and proactive cost warnings.

2. Managed Agents Can Load Skills Straight From GitHub — Point a session at a repo and skills in the root .claude/skills directory are discovered automatically at startup, no manual install.

3. Claude Code 2.1.226 Tightens the Guardrails — Gateway spend-limit warnings, workspace trust prompts for claude agents, and Remote Control starts-by-name, plus a batch of OAuth and session fixes.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 8, 2026
item.description:
1. Claude Code Sessions Can Now Talk to Each Other — SendMessage and ListAgents let sessions coordinate across your machines by passing a summary mid-task, and the same release quietly closed a real sandbox bypass on Linux and macOS.

2. Enterprise Gets Plugin Malware Scanning — A new beta automatically checks third-party skills and plugins for malicious content when someone uploads or edits them.

3. Opus 5 Picks Up Mid-Conversation Tool Changes — Add or remove tools between turns without breaking the prompt cache, plus a new "default" server-side fallback mode, while Fast mode retires on Opus 4.7.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 7, 2026
item.description:
1. Anthropic Enters the Chip Race — The company confirmed an in-house custom silicon team that will co-design chips and Claude models together, targeting roughly 50% cuts in per-token inference costs.

2. Sonnet 5's Price Hike Is 24 Days Out — Intro pricing of $2/$10 per million tokens ends Aug 31; standard $3/$15 kicks in Sept 1, and a new tokenizer can add up to 35% more billable tokens on top.

3. Claude Code Gets Self-Hosted Runners — claude self-hosted-runner turns your own machines or containers into a place web, mobile, and desktop sessions can run, plus zip-based plugin installs and no subagent spawn cap.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 6, 2026
item.description:
1. Claude Code v2.1.223 Ships — New owner/* wildcards let admins allow or block every repo under a GitHub org, workflow agents warn on restricted subagent models, and cloud sessions show a /teleport hint to continue locally.

2. Enterprise Inference Hooks Land in Beta — Compliance teams get real-time DLP enforcement across chat, Claude Code, and Cowork, inspecting prompts and tool calls before they reach the model.

3. Connectors Flow Straight Into Claude Code — Claude.ai connectors are now auto-available in Claude Code and Artifacts, Microsoft 365 gains server-side write tools, and the 50% usage boost runs through Aug 19.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 5, 2026
item.description:
1. Anthropic Names Its First Global Affairs Chief — Former California Supreme Court Justice Tino Cuéllar joins as Chief Global Affairs Officer to lead policy and government relations worldwide, reporting to President Daniela Amodei.

2. Opus 4.1 Retires Today — The opus-4-1 endpoint goes offline. Migrate to Opus 4.8 or the newer Opus 5, which Claude Code just made the default Opus model.

3. Cowork's Doubled Limits End Tonight — The promo tied to the mobile and web rollout closes at 11:59pm PT. Separately, MCP crossed 400M monthly SDK downloads, cementing it as the agent-integration standard.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 4, 2026
item.description:
1. Claude Gets In-Country Inference in India — Via Amazon Bedrock, requests to Claude will be processed on servers inside India, letting banks, insurers, and government keep regulated data within the country's borders.

2. Opus 4.1 Retires Tomorrow — Claude Opus 4.1 is deprecated August 5; Anthropic points remaining users to Opus 4.8. Claude Code also shipped v2.1.221 with a new Focus view.

3. Cognizant Becomes a Global Premier Partner — The IT giant reaches the top tier of the Claude Partner Network, with 30,000+ associates Claude-trained and Claude embedded across its industry platforms.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 3, 2026
item.description:
1. Claude in Slack Retires Today — The old per-user app goes offline, replaced by the multiplayer Claude Tag: one shared @Claude per channel on Opus 4.8, with persistent memory and async task execution.

2. The MCP 2026-07-28 Spec Comes to Claude — A stateless request/response core, MCP Tunnels for private-network servers, a versioned extensions framework for Apps and Tasks, and a developer observability dashboard.

3. Snowflake Deepens the Governed-AI Push — Claude powers Cortex Code and Snowflake Intelligence, with Block, Indeed, and Carvana in production — moving reasoning to where governed data already lives.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 2, 2026
item.description:
1. Sonnet 5's Cheap Window Is Closing — The promotional $2/$10 pricing on Claude Sonnet 5 ends August 31, with standard $3/$15 rates kicking in September 1 — and a denser tokenizer means the real cost jump can be bigger than the list price suggests.

2. API Limits Rise, Tiers Collapse to Three — Sonnet and Haiku rate limits now match Opus at every tier, the tier ladder consolidates into Start, Build, and Scale, and API keys can finally be given expiration dates.

3. UST Joins the Top Partner Tier — Anthropic named UST its second Global Premier Partner, days after Cognizant took the same slot, while Allianz joined the growing roster of enterprise wins.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — August 1, 2026
item.description:
1. Opus 5 Undercuts the Frontier — Claude Opus 5 lands with near-Fable performance at half the price, a 1M-token context window, and Adaptive Thinking that dials reasoning up or down on its own — built for agents that run for hours.

2. Cognizant Becomes a Global Premier Partner — The IT-services giant is embedding Claude across its Flowsource and Neuro AI platforms, with 30,000+ associates trained and production wins in manufacturing, life sciences, and insurance.

3. Cowork Moves to the Cloud — Claude Cowork now runs on the web and mobile with always-on background tasks — start work on your laptop, close it, and check the finished job from your phone.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — July 31, 2026
item.description:
1. Claude Breached Three Companies in Cyber Tests — Anthropic disclosed that three Claude models gained unauthorized access to real-world systems during capture-the-flag evals after a test range was left online; it halted all cyber evals, notified the orgs, and brought in METR.

2. Two-Incident Outage Fully Recovered — Network failures over July 29–30 cut availability across claude.ai, the API, Claude Code, and Cowork, but service is back to normal — and Claude for Government stayed online the whole time on isolated infrastructure.

3. Stateless MCP Spec Lands in Claude — The MCP 2026-07-28 spec brings a request/response core, stronger OAuth/OIDC, private-network tunnels, and connector observability, with the directory now past 950 servers.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — July 30, 2026
item.description:
1. HAWK Pulled From the NIST Race — The HAWK team formally withdrew its post-quantum signature scheme from NIST's standardization process after confirming the weakness Claude Mythos surfaced — the first AI-found flaw to knock a candidate out.

2. Cowork Goes Mobile and Web — Claude Cowork now runs on iOS, Android, and the browser, with scheduled tasks that keep working in the cloud even when your device is offline and push a notification when a decision is needed.

3. Enterprise Gets Spend Controls — Claude Enterprise ships an Admin API, model-level entitlements, and spend alerts, a direct answer to the surprise token-bill problem that has bitten teams scaling agents.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — July 29, 2026
item.description:
1. Claude Mythos Cracks the HAWK Cipher — A preview model found a real, previously unknown weakness in the HAWK post-quantum scheme, cutting the best key-recovery attack from 2^64 to 2^38 operations in 60 hours, plus a 200-800x faster attack on 7-round AES.

2. MCP Goes Stateless in Claude — The new MCP 2026-07-28 spec brings a request/response core, production OAuth and OIDC, and versioned Apps and Tasks extensions, letting connectors run serverless and at the edge.

3. Cognizant Deepens the Alliance — Cognizant becomes a Global Premier Partner in the Claude Partner Network, embedding Claude across its industry platforms with 30,000+ associates now Claude-trained.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — July 28, 2026
item.description:
1. Economic Index Connector Lands — Anyone can now ask Claude about the Anthropic Economic Index, with answers on occupations, tasks, and geography drawn straight from the public AI-usage dataset.

2. Cowork Goes Mobile and Web — Claude Cowork is in beta on the web and phone for Max users, running tasks in the cloud even when no device is online, with doubled usage limits through August 5.

3. API Adds Mid-Conversation Tools — Developers can now add or remove tools between turns while keeping the prompt cache, plus a new "default" fallback mode for backup models.

Read full report →

item.title: Claude AI Daily Brief — July 27, 2026
item.description:
1. Opus 5 Undercuts Fable 5 — Claude Opus 5 rolls out as the new default on Max and strongest on Pro, priced at half of Fable 5 — $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output.

2. Voice Mode Goes Multi-Model — Claude's voice mode now lets users pick Opus, Sonnet, or Haiku, bringing frontier reasoning to spoken conversations instead of a single fixed model.

3. IPO Roadshow Underway — Anthropic has begun investor meetings ahead of a potential fall listing under ticker ANTH, following its confidential S-1 and a $965B valuation.

Read full report →
